sources.name: Ghana Scholarships Authority

seed.title: Ghana Scholarships Authority — Foreign Scholarships for Ghanaian Students
seed.summary: The Ghana Scholarships Authority administers government-funded local and foreign scholarships for Ghanaian students, including bilateral awards to study abroad.

sources.notes: Official Ghanaian government scholarship body (scholarships.gov.gh). Ghana-specific by definition.

sources.name: Chevening Scholarships

seed.title: Chevening Scholarships (Ghana) — Fully Funded UK Master's
seed.summary: Chevening is the UK government's international awards scheme: a fully funded one-year master's degree in the UK for emerging leaders, with a dedicated Ghana allocation.

sources.notes: Ghana-specific page. Requires 2 years (2,800 hours) work experience.

sources.name: DAAD — Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)

seed.title: DAAD EPOS — Development-Related Postgraduate Courses in Germany
seed.summary: DAAD EPOS funds master's and some doctoral study in development-related programmes in Germany for professionals from developing countries, including Ghana, with a monthly stipend, insurance and travel allowance.

sources.notes: Official DAAD scholarship-database entry for EPOS (English). Typically requires ~2 years professional experience; degrees "far above average" — extract exact wording per course.

sources.name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters

seed.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's Scholarships
seed.summary: EU-funded scholarships covering participation costs plus a monthly allowance for integrated master's programmes taught across at least two European universities. Open worldwide, including Ghanaian applicants.

sources.notes: Each consortium sets its own academic entry requirements — many accept a good second-class degree. Apply directly to programmes in the EMJM catalogue.

sources.name: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships

seed.title: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships (UK)
seed.organization: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK
seed.summary: Fully funded one-year master's study in the UK for candidates from low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries (Ghana is eligible): tuition, airfare and a living stipend.

sources.notes: Usually requires at least an upper second (2:1); extract exact wording each cycle — some development themes have flexibility.

seed.title: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships (UK)
seed.organization: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK
seed.summary: Jointly funded fully funded UK master's scholarships for candidates from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries, including Ghana.

sources.name: Australia Awards Scholarships

seed.title: Australia Awards Scholarships
seed.organization: Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
seed.summary: Long-term Australian government awards covering full tuition, travel and living support for study at Australian institutions; eligibility depends on the current country list for Africa.

sources.notes: Official Australia Awards Africa programme site. Verify Ghana inclusion in the current intake each cycle — never assume.

sources.name: MEXT Japanese Government Scholarships

seed.title: MEXT Research (Graduate) Scholarship — Japan
seed.summary: Japanese government scholarship for research students / master's study: tuition, monthly stipend and airfare. Ghanaians apply via the Embassy of Japan in Ghana (embassy recommendation track).

sources.notes: Embassy track for Ghana usually opens around April–May each year.

sources.name: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS)

seed.title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) — Graduate Degrees
seed.organization: National Institute for International Education (NIIED), Korea
seed.summary: Korean government scholarship covering full tuition, monthly allowance, airfare and a Korean language year for graduate study. Ghana is regularly on the invited-country list (embassy and university tracks).

sources.notes: Official Study in Korea portal; GKS notices under K-Scholarship > GKS Notice. GKS typically requires CGPA >= 80% of the scale — extract exact wording; verify against KNUST conversion.

sources.name: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC)

seed.title: Chinese Government Scholarship — Bilateral & University Programmes
seed.summary: Chinese Government Scholarships cover tuition, accommodation and a monthly stipend for degree study in China. Ghanaians can apply via the Ghana Scholarships Authority bilateral track or directly to Chinese universities.

sources.notes: campuschina.org intermittently blocks automated requests (HTTP 412). Failures are recorded and skipped; the Ghana Scholarships Authority bilateral track also covers CSC awards.

sources.name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

seed.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
seed.summary: Comprehensive scholarships (tuition, living costs, mentorship) for young Africans at partner universities in Africa and abroad. Apply through each partner institution.

sources.notes: Application is per partner university (e.g., KNUST, Ashesi, EPFL, McGill, Edinburgh).

sources.name: Clean Air Fund — News & Opportunities
sources.notes: Clean-air philanthropy active in Accra. List parser scans news for open calls.

sources.name: UNEP — Youth & Education Opportunities
sources.notes: UN Environment Programme engagement page; scanned for open programmes.

sources.name: Opportunities for Africans (RSS)
sources.notes: Reputable aggregator for African opportunities. Every item still links to and is verified against its own page; used for discovery, not as ground truth.

sources.name: Opportunity Desk (RSS)
sources.notes: Reputable global opportunity aggregator used for discovery only.

sources.name: DAAD Scholarship Database (Ghana filter)
sources.notes: Inactive by default: the database is JavaScript-rendered and unreliable for plain HTTP parsing. Kept as a registry example of toggling sources.
